advice: Deploy the frontend and the API as two pieces: the frontend as static files or on a platform such as Vercel or Netlify, the API as a container (Fly.io, Render, Railway, Cloud Run).
Keep all configuration in environment variables, with an .env.example listing every name.
Use a managed database with automatic backups, and connect through a pooled connection string.
Put the API behind HTTPS only, and allow your frontend's origin in CORS (not `*`).

protections.title: Rate limiting
protections.why: 1 route(s) that change data can be called as fast as an attacker likes: password guessing, sign-up spam, or running up your bill.
protections.how: Limit requests per user and per IP on these routes: slowapi (FastAPI), Flask-Limiter, express-rate-limit, or @upstash/ratelimit (Next.js / serverless).

protections.title: Security headers
protections.why: Browsers protect your users from clickjacking, mixed content, and injected scripts only when the app sends headers such as Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, and X-Frame-Options.
evidence: full-stack web app; no header setup found in code or hosting config
protections.how: Set them once for every response: helmet (Express), the headers() block in next.config.js, a vercel.json/netlify.toml headers rule, or a small middleware in FastAPI/Flask.

protections.title: Slow password hashing
protections.why: Passwords are handled in the code, and a fast hash (MD5/SHA) is used in the same files: a leaked database could be cracked in hours.
protections.how: Store only argon2 or bcrypt hashes (passlib/pwdlib/bcrypt in Python, bcrypt or argon2 in Node), or use a managed auth service so you never store passwords.

protections.title: Login check on routes that change data
protections.why: 1 route(s) change data with no sign of a login check in the handler, in what it calls, or in app-wide middleware, so anyone on the internet can call them.
protections.how: Check the signed-in user at the top of each handler (or in shared middleware), and check they may act on this record, not just that they are signed in.

# Copy to .env and fill in. Never commit .env.

# used at web/src/pages/Admin.tsx:4 (sent to the browser: must not be secret)
VITE_ADMIN_SECRET=

Dockerfile.why: A slim image that runs as a non-root user, with a health check.
Dockerfile.content:
FROM python:3.12-slim
ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir .
COPY . .
RUN useradd --create-home app
USER app
EXPOSE 8000
HEALTHCHECK CMD python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8000/health', timeout=3)"
CMD ["gunicorn", "-b", "0.0.0.0:8000", "shop.app:app"]

.dockerignore.why: Keeps secrets and bulky folders out of the image.

.github/workflows/ci.yml.why: Runs your tests and Lantern's scanners on every push, so problems are caught before deploy.
.github/workflows/ci.yml.content:
name: ci
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: pip install -e . pytest
      - run: python -m pytest -q
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - run: npm install
        working-directory: web
      - run: npm test --if-present
        working-directory: web
      - name: Lantern security and readiness audit
        run: |
          pip install "lantern[scan] @ git+https://github.com/LittleHenderson/Lantern"
          lantern analyze . --out /tmp/lantern --fail-on high
